title: PURSUE Releases Sixth Tranche of 71 UAP Files, Including AAWSAP Warp-Drive Studies and 1952 Tremonton Film
detail: The Department of War published a sixth tranche of declassified UAP files at war.gov/UFO — 71 files (55 PDFs, 15 videos, 1 audio recording), 67 from the Defense Department and 4 from local law enforcement in Colorado, with 64 of the 71 containing redactions. Contents span 1952-2025 and include: 37 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents from the 2008-2012 Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP) studying warp drives, wormholes, antigravity, and negative-mass propulsion, which the department cautioned 'should not be read as implying current validation of the concepts discussed'; a 2010 38-page study of 'anomalous acute and subacute field effects on human biological tissues' describing three antenna engineers with radiation-like symptoms after aerospace-related incidents; a declassified 1952 Tremonton, Utah color film of 10-14 bright objects shot by Navy Chief Warrant Officer Delbert C. Newhouse, officially attributed to 'pillow balloons' though a contemporaneous General Mills analyst called them 'somewhat too bright'; a one-hour 1952 audio interview with Air Force Capt. Edward Ruppelt on Project Blue Book, noting roughly 20% of 800 examined cases remained unexplained; four October 2023 Colorado law-enforcement cellphone videos of silent red/blue/green flashing lights; and 2022-2025 infrared military sensor footage from the Middle East, the Yellow Sea, and the East China Sea. Tranches released May 8, May 22, June 12, July 10, and Aug 7 had brought the prior PURSUE total to 379 files; this release brings the cumulative total to roughly 450.
confidenceReason: Official war.gov press release (tier 1) with matching independent tier-2 reporting (CBS News, FOX 32) on file counts, sources, and document contents.
